subject: ElevateDocs discovery: qualification, model recommendations & prompt intake
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@elevatedocs.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: First call recap: ElevateDocs x Redwood

Thanks for the call today — quick recap from my side and a couple asks:

What we covered:
- Use case: ElevateDocs will add a Q&A assistant for legal intake documents (contracts, NDAs, memos). Goal is to reduce reviewer time for first-pass triage.
- Volume: ~6k docs/month initially, spikes during M&A windows. Mostly English, some Spanish.
- Sensitivity: high (PII, contracts). Data residence: US.

Asks from us:
1) Can you send model recommendations and a short benchmark (latency / expected cost per 1k tokens) for the baseline prompts we discussed?
2) Please share a prompt intake template we can use to send representative examples and edge cases (we can include up to ~80 prompts initially).
3) Redaction guidance: what do you recommend we send as-is vs. redact before upload?

I attached the call recording and will put together a quick list of sample prompts this week.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Product, ElevateDocs
alex.turner@elevatedocs.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: call-recording-20270315.mp3 (audio/stub)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@elevatedocs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: First call recap: ElevateDocs x Redwood

Alex — great to meet. Follow-up and next steps below. I also attached a short prompt intake template (CSV) so you can drop samples in.

Quick recommendations (starter configurations):
- Model family: rw-instruct-7b-q4 (balanced quality / cost) for initial eval; rw-llm-13b-8k for higher-accuracy, longer-context batches.
- Safety/PII profile: run inference through our private deployment (VPC) for initial tests; enable token-level redaction hooks and automatic prefix caching.

Benchmarks we expect (ballpark for your workload on dedicated capacity):
- rw-instruct-7b-q4: median tail latency ~85ms / token; ~ $0.004 per 1k tokens (batched sampling).
- rw-llm-13b-8k: median tail latency ~150ms / token; ~ $0.012 per 1k tokens.
Links: benchmark summary (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-benchmarks (see "ED-legal-quickbench.pdf").

Prompt intake + edge case guidance:
- Please provide 60–100 representative prompts, prioritized by frequency. Include: 1) short factual queries ("What clause limits indemnity?"), 2) multi-step reasoning ("Summarize termination obligations across clauses"), 3) noisy inputs (OCR artifacts), 4) bilingual examples.
- Label each prompt with: expected answer type (span / short / summary), sensitive_fields (SSN, bank account, names), redaction_needed (yes/no).
- For PII: we recommend sending redacted originals when possible; if you must include PII, mark it and we will run redaction hooks on upload.

Mutual action plan (proposal):
1) You send CSV of prompts + 3 representative documents by end of week (use attached template).
2) We run a 1-week pilot on dedicated capacity using rw-instruct-7b-q4 and rw-llm-13b-8k; deliver eval report with accuracy, latency, and safety regressions.
3) Review results and decide on production model + deployment (hosted vs. private).

Next steps: please upload the CSV and any sample docs to the Drive link or share via DocuSign / secure share. If you'd like, we can schedule a 60-min tech workshop with our infra engineer (Ben) to walk through redaction hooks and S3 transfer.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_prompt_intake_template.csv (CSV stub)

Adding a few technical notes for the pilot and evaluation metrics:

Eval & metrics (suggested):
- Quality: exact-match for span extraction, ROUGE-L / chrF for summaries, and a human-eval sample for edge cases (n=150).
- Safety: false-positive PII masking rate, false-negative leakage rate.
- Performance: p50/p90/p99 latency per token and per-request; throughput target 200 rps for batch windows.

Quantization / inference tips:
- Start with q4f16 quant for rw-instruct-7b-q4; it'll keep latency low while preserving answer fidelity for extraction tasks.
- For longer-context legal reasoning, try rw-llm-13b-8k with KV cache and 8k context stride — we can enable prefix caching for repeated templates.

Data sharing and security:
- For PII-containing samples, please put them into the secure folder in the DocuSign NDA flow (link below) or share via our SFTP.

I'll be on the tech workshop if you want to book it; propose Thu 2027-03-25 10:00 PT.

—Ben
